## September 17 source discovery and audit

The cycle screened five candidate identities not already maintained under those exact identities: **Biblioteca Virtual del Patrimonio Bibliográfico (BVPB)**, **Biblioteca Virtual de Prensa Histórica (BVPH)**, **Biblioteca Digital de Andalucía**, **Biblioteca Digital de Castilla y León**, and **Memòria Digital de Catalunya**.

BVPB, BVPH, and Biblioteca Digital de Andalucía received full audits. BVPB passed for a deliberately narrow first-party link-only integration. Its Ministry of Culture presentation describes open/free discovery of digitized bibliographic heritage, while its current legal guidance distinguishes mostly-public-domain underlying works from record-specific rights on digital reproductions; the majority-license statement for digital objects was therefore not generalized into a collection-wide redistribution claim. A separately identified bounded set of 6,769 older Registro de la Propiedad Intelectual works was treated only as evidence that explicit public-domain subsets exist, not as evidence for the whole BVPB corpus.

BVPH also passed a rights/access review for possible future link-only discovery: the current Ministry presentation exposes a large historical-press collection, while its legal guidance likewise requires record-specific licensing rather than a blanket reuse assumption. It was deferred this cycle to avoid admitting two closely related Ministry heritage families at once and to preserve a distinct press-oriented reader task for a later cycle.

Biblioteca Digital de Andalucía has strong first-party public-domain heritage language, but the actual reader-path origin returned a 502 from this operating environment during bounded verification. The cycle did not route around or bypass that failure and deferred admission until the public reader path can be independently reproduced.

Biblioteca Digital de Castilla y León and Memòria Digital de Catalunya were screened and retained as future candidates. The available evidence indicates item/edition-specific rights boundaries rather than a safe generic redistribution assumption; Memòria Digital de Catalunya in particular visibly mixes public-domain, Creative Commons, in-copyright, and rights-reserved records. Any later integration must preserve those record-level distinctions.

### Passing integration: BVPB

Pull request #176 added **BVPB Spanish Heritage Discovery Starter** as the **31st maintained source family**. It contains exactly three reviewed first-party navigation routes: the BVPB home/collection entry point, the advanced catalog search surface, and the current legal/reuse guidance. The source stores only destination URLs plus WebNR-authored labels/descriptions. It does not mirror catalog records, scans, PDFs, JPEGs, OCR, OAI/SRU responses, metadata, credentials, account state, or rights statements, and it does not add a crawler, remote-search runtime, API client, proxy, or background synchronization.

A richer BVPB adapter remains gated on a separate source-specific audit of exact item endpoints, record-level rights/attribution, OAI/SRU terms, browser transport, file identity, update/deletion semantics, paging/cadence, resource/failure limits, supported formats, and versioned fixtures. `Web Novel Discussion Radar Starter` remains unchanged at **12** link-only routes.
